content.title: About
content.content: Canned lentil soup is a ready‑to‑eat soup made from whole red or green lentils, vegetables, spices and broth, sealed in an airtight can. It retains the nutritional qualities of lentils and is convenient for quick meals.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Lentils are one of the oldest legume crops, cultivated for over 8,000 years.
Canning allows the soup to stay shelf‑stable for 2–3 years without added preservatives.
Lentil soup is considered a comfort food in many cultures, from Russia to India.
A typical can contains about 300–400 g of finished soup, ideal for a single serving on the go.
Lentils are rich in plant protein and iron, making them popular among vegetarians.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: Lentils provide roughly 9 g of protein per 100 g, supporting muscle maintenance.

items.title: High in dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber aids digestion and helps regulate blood sugar levels.

items.title: Contains iron and folate
items.content: These micronutrients are essential for blood formation and anemia prevention.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: The soup contains minimal saturated fat, suitable for low‑fat diets.

items.title: Provides antioxidants
items.content: Phytonutrients in lentils help combat free radicals.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Canned foods often have added salt; people with hypertension should choose low‑sodium versions.

items.title: Legume allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to lentils.

items.title: Anti‑nutrients
items.content: Raw lentils contain phytic acid, but the canning process greatly reduces it.

items.title: Heat treatment
items.content: Heat the soup to a rolling boil to ensure any potential bacteria are destroyed.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Open the can, pour the contents into a pot and bring to a boil for 5–7 minutes. Add fresh herbs, a squeeze of lemon, or a drizzle of olive oil for extra flavor. The soup can be enjoyed on its own or as part of a larger meal.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store unopened cans in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. After opening, transfer leftovers to an airtight container and keep refrigerated, consuming within 3–4 days.
